coverage: Monday run, 28 Sep 2026 ~07:02-07:20 SGT. Markets are all closed/pre-open at run time: US closed all weekend (last close Fri 25 Sep, reopens Monday evening SGT), HKEX/SGX open at 09:30/09:00 SGT today, JPX at 09:00 JST (08:00 SGT), and KRX reopens today after its 4-day Chuseok closure (last close Wed 23 Sep). No new trading session has occurred anywhere since Friday, so equity/breadth/sentiment readings are re-verified rather than re-measured. The dominant development remains the Iran/Hormuz standoff: Trump said Sat 26 Sep he expects renewed talks 'this week,' but Iran's FM Araghchi hardened Tehran's line Sun 27 Sep -- no formal mediator response received, won't soften conditions, calls Trump's remarks 'contradictory' -- pointing toward the ~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep deadline lapsing without a deal. Oil's reaction diverged sharply rather than moving as one block: Brent plunged 5.4% to $98.70 Sunday on speculative talk-hope (a war-premium unwind, not an actual supply change) while WTI rose 1.3% to $93.58 as the physical Hormuz constraint held -- this run's price spine also corrects a Saturday-run framing error that had assumed both benchmarks spiked together. Gold ($4,294.40, -0.62% Sun) and silver ($64.18, -0.10% Sun) gave back a slice of Friday's bounce (gold +0.54%, silver +1.24% Fri) rather than either 'extending a pullback' or 'reversing a dip' as two of this run's own draft files inconsistently framed it -- the accurate read, from the raw OHLC, is a solid Friday bounce partly unwound over the weekend, a genuine safe-haven-playbook anomaly given how hard Iran's line got. tldr: Iran's self-imposed Hormuz deadline (~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) looks set to lapse without a deal -- Iran's FM hardened Sunday's line even as Trump talked up 'renewed talks this week' -- and oil is pricing that as a split verdict, not a single direction: Brent plunged 5.4% to $98.70 on talk-hope while WTI rose 1.3% to $93.58 on the still-unresolved physical chokepoint risk.

Gold and silver gave back a slice of Friday's solid bounce over the weekend (-0.6%/-0.1%) even as the Iran line hardened -- the safe-haven playbook isn't firing cleanly right now, worth watching rather than assuming a clean war-premium trade for the levered silver/miner sleeve.
